problem: Prior VLN-CE methods that imagine future environments use either predicted RGB images (DreamWalker, lacking high-level semantics) or NeRF-rendered semantic features (HNR, lacking appearance cues such as color and texture). NeRF rendering is also very slow.
motivation: Human perception of unseen environments combines intuitive appearance with high-level semantics, and VLN-CE agents suffer from occlusions and blind spots. 3DGS renders fast, while NeRF volume rendering gives accurate ray-to-pixel semantics, so combining them could give richer and faster future-view representations.
key_idea: Pre-train a generalizable 3DGS+NeRF hybrid that renders 360° future views, using 3DGS for images and features and NeRF for semantic features, and fuses them into a future-node representation for waypoint scoring.
insight: Fusing multi-source future representations (RGB via 3DGS, features via 3DGS, semantic features via NeRF) beats either branch alone: Table 3 shows Base 57.6 SR, NeRF-only 61.4, 3DGS-only 61.9, STQ+STU 62.4. The module also plugs into ETPNav (SR 57.2 to 58.9) and HNR (60.7 to 62.4), and it renders about 63x faster than HNR (0.036s vs 2.21s).
method: Neural point initialization: project 12 panoramic RGB-D views into a colored point cloud B and a CLIP-ViT-B feature cloud M (with view direction and scale), accumulated online over visited and current nodes; a pretrained waypoint predictor proposes candidate nodes.

Search-Then-Query (STQ) in 3DGS: a KD-tree over coarse occupancy grids finds K-nearest neighbors, then points at local density maxima are kept to sparsify B; a Pcd U-Net (SA + point-voxel conv + FP) yields neural descriptors, and MLP heads regress rotation, scale and opacity to give image Gaussians (colors) and feature Gaussians (descriptors).

STQ in NeRF: for each ray sample, K-nearest feature-cloud neighbors within a 1 m radius are aggregated by inverse-distance weighting (MLP φ1); MLPs φ2 and φ3 regress view-dependent feature radiance and density.

Separate-Then-United (STU) rendering: the 3DGS rasterizer renders image I_g and feature map F_g, and cross-attention fuses CLIP-encoded F_g into I_g; NeRF volume rendering (256 samples over 0-10 m) renders feature F_f, which a Transformer encodes.

Fusion and navigation: the 3DGS and NeRF embeddings are aggregated per view, 12 views are average-pooled into a future node, and an FFN scores candidate and future nodes on the ETPNav-style topological map (visited nodes masked).
Training: pre-train the renderer on 800 HM3D scenes with L1+L2+SSIM on images and a cosine feature loss against CLIP; then train the navigator with soft-target cross-entropy, initialized from ETPNav.

setting.backbone: ETPNav-based topological planner (transformer) + CLIP-ViT-B/16 + generalizable 3DGS/NeRF renderer (trained)
setting.training_data: Renderer pre-trained on 800 HM3D training scenes (20k episodes); navigator trained on R2R-CE (20k episodes) or RxR-CE (100k episodes), initialized from ETPNav weights
setting.action_space: low-level (forward 0.25 m, turn 15°) executed via a waypoint predictor with topological-map candidate nodes
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R-CE, RxR-CE on Matterport3D; HM3D for pre-training)

numbers_note: The R2R-CE val-unseen ablation tables (A5, B4, E5) print SR 62.4 / SPL 51.1 / OSR 70.0, slightly different from the rounded main-table values of 62 / 51 / 70. The main-table values are used above.
results: UnitedVLN reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 62 / SPL 51 / NE 4.29 and test-unseen SR 59 / SPL 49, beating HNR (val-unseen SR 61, SPL 51; test-unseen SR 58, SPL 50) by about 1 point SR; test-unseen SPL is 1 point below HNR and BEVBert. On RxR-CE val-unseen it gets SR 57.7 versus HNR 56.4, and rendering is about 63x faster than HNR.
limitations: 3DGS popping artifacts and Gaussian switching can lose fine detail (stated).
Gains over HNR are small (about 1 SR point), and test-unseen SPL is slightly lower than HNR and BEVBert.
It needs a two-stage pipeline (renderer pre-training plus agent training) and depends on a pretrained waypoint predictor.
